rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 1 "Big Idea" (line 6) is the shortest chunk at 12 words but carries a complete standalone claim: "Trust isn't watching harder. It's verification you can run without being there." — not a wait-state or context-dependent fragment. Every other chunk carries its own bullets/paragraphs with a self-carrying claim.

Checked each header against its chunk's content: "Sharpen the skill from evidence" (chunk 5) content is the sharpen prompt itself; "Clear the session" (chunk 7) content is the wrap-and-clear sequence; "Bring to Module 4" (chunk 10) content states the one task to bring. No header is contradicted by its own chunk.

No "Not X. Not Y. Z." triples, no anaphora/epistrophe triples, no self-grading superlatives, no abstraction-noun stacks, no empty-leg verb triplets anywhere in the body. The two bolded floor/ceiling sentences (chunk 2 line 14: "A feature you could ship in a few hours. Not a quarter-long epic."; chunk 10 line 95: "One scoped task you'd send off rather than nudge bit by bit: a real slice. Bigger than a typo-fix, smaller than an epic.") are single "X. Not Y." pairs matching the §34 task-sizing shape verbatim, not the banned triple construction. "Too small... Too large..." (chunk 2 line 12) is a contrasting pair, not a triple.
